target_customer: Publishers and developers who need rich embeds and link previews on their sites
problem: Each site needed custom code to embed media from many services. Embedly provided one API turning links into embeds, extracted content and resized images.
business_model: Usage-based API with a free tier and paid plans
product_category: Link embedding and content extraction API

founders.name: Sean Creeley
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him twice; no background in opened sources.

founders.name: Art Gibson
founders.background_notes: Named as Arthur Gibson on the YC page and Art Gibson by VentureBeat. No background found.

competitors.name: Oohembed
competitors.what: Gateway to non-oEmbed sites; users were later redirected to embed.ly

technical_complexity.rationale: Maintaining parsers and provider integrations for 100+ sites, plus scale to millions of URLs per month; ongoing integration work more than novel research.

defensibility.rationale: Customers integrated the API, but open oEmbed standards and later open-source or cheaper alternatives such as Iframely limited lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it early. Medium, an existing customer, acquired it in August 2016 and kept it running as a product.

market_need_then: Publishers needed embed support across many services in 2010; the company reported about 4 million URLs a month by July 2010 per a 2011 TechCrunch piece.

branding.domain_note: Used the embed.ly domain, a .ly name that reads as the product name; purchase history not found.
branding.community_and_virality: Trusted by list on site includes Medium; coverage as a developer tool.

brand_strength.rationale: Name describes the function, the .ly domain is memorable and customers such as the New York Times, Reddit and The Guardian are named on its pages, but no source shows brand driven growth.

pivots.to: Embed, Extract and Display product suite
pivots.why: Expanded beyond embeds to extraction and image resizing; TechCrunch coverage title; reason not detailed

outcome_analysis: Embedly, a two person Boston startup, raised small seed rounds totaling about 700 thousand dollars per VentureBeat from Betaworks, SV Angel, Salesforce Ventures and others and served large publishers via its API. Medium, already a customer, acquired it in August 2016 for undisclosed terms and kept all 10 employees. The outcome was a small, capital efficient exit with a customer buying a critical supplier.
notes: The June 2011 round title says another 450 thousand dollars, implying an earlier round; aggregators list 250 thousand in August 2010 (with a16z, unverified) and totals from 770 thousand to 1.04 million dollars, which conflict, so only the TechCrunch round is recorded. VentureBeat states 700 thousand total and lists Y Combinator, SV Angel and Salesforce Ventures among investors; round dates for those are unknown. The November 2012 date for the product suite is not sourced exactly, so the pivot date is approximate. Oohembed competitor entry has no dated source.
